verdict.rationale: React's own docs say that on the server it can start streaming HTML while data is still being fetched, progressively filling in the remaining content (react-docs-6). That is a first-party capability for a responsive, progressive loading UI around server data. Async data-fetching components are framed as something frameworks implement (react-docs-7), so they add little first-party weight, and the pack never names Suspense, a resource/use primitive, or treating loaded data as reactive state. missing for 10: explicit documentation of Suspense boundaries and fallback UI, a resource/data-reading primitive, evidence that server-loaded data behaves as reactive state, and independent or hands-on corroboration.
